title: What do AMMCreate and AMMDeposit do on XRPL, and what is the maximum AMM trading fee?
abstract: Sourced guide to creating an XRPL automated market maker, its trading-fee range and reserve cost, and the deposit modes that return liquidity-provider tokens.
body:
According to the XRPL AMMCreate reference, AMMCreate creates a new Automated Market Maker instance for a pair of assets, and its TradingFee is at most 1000, a 1% trading fee. The pair can be fungible tokens or XRP. [1]

TradingFee is in units of 1/100,000, with a minimum of 0. AMMCreate must destroy at least the incremental owner reserve amount, currently 0.2 XRP. One or both assets can be tokens but at most one can be XRP, they cannot share a currency code and issuer, and token issuers must have Default Ripple enabled. A second AMM for the same pair fails with tecDUPLICATE. [1]

According to the XRPL AMMDeposit reference, AMMDeposit deposits funds into an AMM instance and receives the AMM's liquidity provider tokens, called LP tokens. Flags select the mode: tfTwoAsset deposits specified amounts of both assets, tfSingleAsset deposits one asset, tfLPToken is a double-asset deposit that receives a specified amount of LP tokens, tfOneAssetLPToken is the single-asset equivalent, tfLimitLPToken sets an effective price, and tfTwoAssetIfEmpty is for an empty pool. A successful deposit creates a trust line to the AMM account, with limit 0, to hold the LP tokens. [2]

Author interpretation: LP tokens are the depositor's claim on the pool, so an agent that deposits should record its LP token balance and the reserve for the new trust line, not only the assets it sent. Neither reference promises a return. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [1][2]
